focus: P11: Lug-First Memory — capture user direction as principle
action: Added P11 to wai-principles.md and appended signal lug signal-p11-lug-first-memory-20260322. P11 formalizes that work intent, decisions, and sub-agent prompts belong in lugs, not task tools or markdown files.
thinking: The user's direction was grounded in a live demonstration: the subagent prompt was recoverable from lug m8n3p7q2r6s4 workflow.subagent_prompt after session interruption. This is exactly the P1 (Persistence) corollary but specific to the choice of storage medium. P1 says 'nothing survives without explicit save' — P11 says 'save in the right place: lugs, not tasks or md'. The signal needs high impact (9) because it directly governs AI behavior across all sessions. The principles file is the right canonical home. wai-rules.md references skill files for behavioral rules so no update needed there.
decisions: P11 is the right framing: positive statement of where work belongs, not just what to avoid
Signal impact=9: governs behavior across all future sessions and agents
No wai-rules.md update needed — it delegates to skill files
insights: The demonstration was more persuasive than any abstract rule: the session interrupted, the lug survived, the work resumed
evolution: orientation -> execution: captured user direction as durable principle and signal

focus: Dogfood P11 lug — review and improve via cold-start subagent
action: Dispatched cold-start subagent to review signal-p11-lug-first-memory-20260322. Subagent found 4 real gaps. Implemented all fixes: updated P11 in wai-principles.md and updated lug description in WAI-Lugs.jsonl.
thinking: The subagent review was genuinely useful — it caught that the lug assumed system knowledge a cold agent doesn't have (what is a lug, where does it live, what is the wakeup protocol). The key improvements: define lug structure upfront, front-load the failure mode (lead with 'the next agent starts blind'), add explicit trigger ('about to use TaskCreate? stop'), add minimal concrete example with workflow.subagent_prompt shown in context. The dogfood protocol works — a lug written for agents who know the system is not the same as one that works for agents who don't.
